Seafood Linguine for the Feast of the Seven Fishes

Served at: Christmas Eve

Serves 6-8Prep 30 minCook 40 min

The Feast of the Seven Fishes, or La Vigilia, is a cherished Italian-American Christmas Eve tradition where families gather to enjoy a grand meal composed entirely of fish and seafood, abstaining from meat. This vibrant Seafood Linguine, brimming with fresh shrimp, mussels, and calamari in a light tomato-wine sauce, serves as a magnificent and essential centerpiece, symbolizing the abundance and celebratory spirit of the holiday.

Ingredients

  • 1 pound (450 g) linguine
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) olive oil
  • 6 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 ml) red pepper flakes, or to taste
  • 1 cup (240 ml) dry white wine
  • 28 ounces (794 g) canned crushed tomatoes
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) fresh parsley, chopped, divided
  • 1 pound (450 g) large shrimp, peeled and deveined
  • 2 pounds (900 g) mussels, scrubbed and de-bearded
  • 1 pound (450 g) calamari rings and tentacles, cleaned
  • Salt, to taste
  • Black pepper, to taste
  • 1 lemon, for serving (optional)

Method

  1. Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil for the linguine. Cook linguine according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 1 cup (240 ml) of the pasta water.
  2. While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and red pepper flakes, cooking for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, being careful not to burn the garlic.
  3. Pour in the white wine and bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Let it reduce by about half, approximately 3-5 minutes.
  4. Add the crushed tomatoes and half of the chopped parsley to the skillet. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld.
  5. Add the mussels to the sauce, cover the skillet, and cook for 3-5 minutes, or until the mussels open. Discard any mussels that do not open.
  6. Stir in the shrimp and calamari. Cook for another 3-5 minutes, or until the shrimp are pink and opaque and the calamari is tender. Be careful not to overcook the seafood.
  7. Add the drained linguine to the skillet with the seafood sauce. Toss to combine, adding a splash of the reserved pasta water if the sauce seems too thick.
  8. Garnish with the remaining fresh parsley. Serve immediately, with lemon wedges on the side if desired.

Tips

  • For an even richer flavor, consider adding a splash of clam juice or fish stock along with the white wine.
  • Feel free to customize the seafood; scallops, clams, or firm white fish chunks can also be added to this versatile dish.
  • Ensure all seafood is fresh and properly cleaned for the best taste and texture in your Feast of the Seven Fishes.
